sections.skill: Choose protective packaging and track damage rate

questions.prompt: What does packaging do besides protect the item?
questions.intro: PACKAGING protects products in shipping and shapes the customer's first impression. Match packaging to the item: fragile items need cushioning and a sturdy box; flat items need stiff mailers. Test by packing a few items and shipping them to yourself or a friend. Include packaging cost (box, filler, tape, labels) in cost per item. Track DAMAGE RATE: damaged orders / total orders. A small increase in packaging cost can be worth it if it cuts expensive replacements.

questions.prompt: 15 damaged of 500. What is the damage rate?
questions.intro: Damage rate = damaged orders / total orders. Cost of damage = damaged orders x replacement cost. Example: 300 orders with 12 damaged is 12 / 300 = 4 percent; at 18 dollars to replace each, damage costs 12 x 18 = 216 dollars. Compare this with the extra cost of better packaging across all orders. The cheaper total wins, and fewer unhappy customers is a bonus.
